title: AI Unlocked: Finance & Accounting
blurb: For accountants, analysts, and finance teams: close-and-reporting acceleration, Excel/Sheets AI mastery, FP&A and analysis workflows, the finance-AI tool market compared, and the controls/audit-trail discipline regulators expect.

modules.d: From bookkeeping to FP&A — the value map and the control mindset.
modules.body:
Landscape

  • Bookkeeping categorization, reconciliation matching, invoice processing: heavily automated already.
  • Reporting narratives, variance analysis, forecasting support: the new frontier.
  • Unchanged: professional judgment, controls ownership, and signatures — AI outputs enter workpapers only with review evidence.
House rule: numbers come from systems; AI narrates and checks — it never invents a figure.
The OECD AI Principles — the first intergovernmental AI standard, adopted by 40+ nations — define the goal as "trustworthy AI": innovation with accountability. Finance professionals already speak that language; controls, audit trails, and evidence are your native tongue. This course just adds horsepower.

opts: Narrate and check numbers that come from systems

modules.d: Copilot in Excel and Gemini in Sheets — formulas, cleanup, and models at speed.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Formula generation and explanation ("write and explain the XLOOKUP/SUMIFS for…").
  • Data cleanup: messy exports → structured tables with documented transformation steps.
  • Model scaffolding: three-statement and budget models drafted, then YOUR assumptions and checks.
  • Error hunting: "Audit this sheet for circularities, hardcodes, and inconsistent formulas."
plAIbox™: rebuild one recurring workbook with AI assistance; document time saved and every correction made.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a senior FP&A analyst. Here are my actuals vs budget [paste table]. Draft the variance commentary: what moved, plausible drivers to verify operationally, a bridge narrative for the board pack, and three questions the CFO will ask — with the analysis I should prepare for each. Do not invent any figure.

modules.t: Tool Study: The Finance AI Market
modules.d: QuickBooks/Xero AI vs close platforms vs FP&A tools vs spreadsheet AI — fit by firm size.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • SMB ledgers (QuickBooks Intuit Assist, Xero JAX): categorization, reconciliation, cash-flow insights inside the ledger — included in subscriptions.
  • Close/AP automation (Ramp/Bill-class, FloQast-class): receipt matching, approvals, close checklists; per-entity pricing; mid-market sweet spot.
  • FP&A platforms (Datarails/Cube-class): Excel-native consolidation + AI narratives; for teams outgrowing raw sheets.
  • General LLMs + spreadsheet AI: the analyst's daily leverage at minimal cost.
  • Selection: data sensitivity terms, audit-trail features, integration with your ledger, and per-seat economics.

modules.d: Variance stories, forecasts, and board packs — with the analyst in charge.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Variance analysis: actuals vs budget tables → drafted explanations you verify against operational facts.
  • Forecast support: driver identification, scenario tables (best/base/worst — the operator technique, financialized).
  • Board pack narratives and KPI commentary; data storytelling for non-finance executives.
  • The month-end close narrative (our SMB methodology, corporate edition).

modules.d: Review evidence, data confidentiality, and regulator expectations.
modules.body:
Discipline

  • Every AI-assisted workpaper carries: source data reference, prompt used, reviewer sign-off.
  • Client/company financial data only in tools with enterprise data terms; consumer tools get anonymized extracts at most.
  • Fraud-detection assistance and its false-positive etiquette; auditor expectations for AI-touched processes documented.

opts: Source reference, prompt, and reviewer sign-off
